beats.beat: Elin spots racks of leaves with bright silver veins that smear faintly when she rubs her thumb across them.
Garret confirms it is berry dye painted over unripe veins, not true silvering.
Cornered, Jasper admits the mature trees nearby are stripped bare and he started painting veins for quota and his mother's medicine.
A neighbor runs up with news the shipment already left before dawn on Kettering's caravan, a full day's lead.

turn.note: Ends on the news of the caravan's full-day lead, forcing a chase and reintroducing Dessa, which sets up chapter 4 directly.

listenability: 'The fullers grey wool with it.' uses 'grey' as a verb mid-sentence, which a listener may parse as an adjective first; reword to 'The fullers use it to dye wool grey.'

generic_prose.quote: he did not pretend to be surprised to see them
generic_prose.replace_with: show his foreknowledge concretely, e.g. he is already holding the dye-crock rather than a bucket of water

generic_prose.quote: He looked at the racks rather than at either of them.
generic_prose.replace_with: a specific guilty gesture — coiling a cord, wiping a thumbnail — rather than a generic avoidance beat

trope_note: Serves the rule-that-must-not-be-broken and the apprentice tropes directly through the dye reveal and Elin's unsanctioned rub-test; the thing-nobody-has-studied trope is held back for chapter 4's breath test, which is correct pacing.
fixes: Chapter runs noticeably over its 450-word target; cut the redundant beat 'He set the bucket down and stayed where he was.' since the bucket was already established the line before.
Replace 'and he did not pretend to be surprised to see them' with a concrete physical tell rather than a stated absence of surprise.
Replace 'He looked at the racks rather than at either of them.' with a specific guilty gesture unique to Jasper.
Reword 'The fullers grey wool with it' for clarity on listen-through, e.g. 'The fullers use it to dye wool grey.'
Consider compressing the two narrator paragraphs after the break (cart's early departure and the caravan's schedule) into one to recover word count without losing the beat.

findings.quote: The sky had gone grey over the stumps before anybody spoke about what to do.
findings.note: The sentence after a scene break has to say when or where we now are — it is the only cue a listener gets that time has passed.
